abstract: INTRODUCTION: Evidence from previous studies has suggested there may be physical and mental changes in health among testicular cancer survivors. No studies have been conducted in the United States, however. METHODS: Study participants were initially enrolled in the US Servicemen's Testicular Tumor Environmental and Endocrine Determinants (STEED) study between 2002 and 2005. A total of 246 TGCT (testicular germ cell tumor) cases and 236 non-testicular cancer controls participated in the current study, and completed a self-administered questionnaire. Mean time since diagnosis for cases was 14 years, and no less than five for all cases. Component scores determined from responses to questions about physical and mental health on SF36 were tabulated to yield two summary measures, physical component scores (PCS), and mental component scores (MCS). Component and summary scores were normalized to a score of 50 with a standard deviation of 10 by a linear T-score transformation. RESULTS: Overall, cases may not suffer greatly in different quality of life than controls. When all cases and controls are compared, TGCT cases had lower PCS (mean: 51.9 95% CI: 50.6-53.2, P value: 0.037) than controls (mean: 53.6 95% CI: 52.7-54.6). MCS were not significantly different (P value: 0.091). In multivariate analyses, several physical health components were worse for TGCT cases such as role-physical (OR 1.19, 95% CI: 1.01-1.39) and general health (OR 1.26, 95% CI: 1.07-1.49) compared to controls. However, TGCT cases treated with chemotherapy had lower PCS (cases: 50.2, 95% CI: 47.6-52.8; controls: 53.6, 95% CI: 52.7-54.6, P value: 0.0032) and MCS (cases: 49.3, 95% CI: 46.5-52.1; controls: 52.0, 95% CI: 50.9-53.2, P value: 0.039). TGCT cases who received treatments other than chemotherapy did not differ from controls in either PCS or MCS. DISCUSSION: Physical and general health limitations may affect testicular cancer survivors. Men treated with chemotherapy, however, may be most likely to suffer adverse health outcomes due to a combination of body-wide effects on physical and mental factors which affect various aspects of physical health, mental health, and overall quality of life. And in particular, physical functioning, role-physical, and general health are strongly affected.
abstract_ja: 序論：先行研究では、精巣がんの生存者に身体的・精神的な変化がみられる可能性が示唆されている。しかし米国での研究はこれまでなかった。方法：研究参加者は2002年から2005年にかけて米国兵役者精巣腫瘍環境・内分泌決定因子（STEED）研究に登録された。本研究には精巣胚細胞腫瘍（TGCT）の症例246例と非精巣がん対照236例が参加し、自己記入式質問票に回答した。症例の診断からの平均期間は14年で、いずれも最低5年であった。SF-36の身体的・精神的健康に関する質問への回答から、身体コンポーネントスコア（PCS）と精神コンポーネントスコア（MCS）を算出した。各コンポーネントおよびサマリースコアは線形Tスコア変換により、平均50、標準偏差10に標準化された。結果：全体として、症例は対照と比べて生活の質が大きく低下しているわけではなかった。全症例と対照を比較すると、TGCT症例のPCSは対照（平均53.6、95%CI 52.7-54.6）より低かった（平均51.9、95%CI 50.6-53.2、P=0.037）。MCSには有意差がなかった（P=0.091）。多変量解析では、TGCT症例は対照と比べて役割（身体）（OR 1.19、95%CI 1.01-1.39）や全般的健康感（OR 1.26、95%CI 1.07-1.49）が不良であった。化学療法を受けたTGCT症例はPCS（症例50.2、95%CI 47.6-52.8、対照53.6、95%CI 52.7-54.6、P=0.0032）およびMCS（症例49.3、95%CI 46.5-52.1、対照52.0、95%CI 50.9-53.2、P=0.039）が低かった。化学療法以外の治療を受けたTGCT症例は、PCSもMCSも対照と差がなかった。考察：身体的・全般的な健康上の制限が精巣がんの生存者に影響を及ぼす可能性がある。化学療法を受けた男性は、身体的要因と精神的要因の両方に及ぶ全身的な影響が組み合わさり、有害な転帰を生じやすい可能性がある。特に身体機能、役割（身体）、全般的健康感が強く影響を受ける。
